findings.caption: The live culinary universe: every ingredient the product can recognize.
Expanded from the original 463 species nodes by adding 232 recipe-derived ingredients.
About one-fifth of ingredient→gene edges are lab-measured; the rest are structure-inferred.
On a hard Murcko-scaffold split, nearest-neighbor inference recovers a true target in the top-10 ~86% of the time.
Only 1.3% of random null ingredient gene-sets light up any pathway at q<0.1 — the enrichment test is conservative, not inflated.
Across 400 recipes, leave-one-out redundancy averages ~0.90 — most ingredients are partially interchangeable.
In a spice curry, removing turmeric barely moves the body-message vector (~2% change) — spices are redundant with each other.
Unique food compounds linked to ingredients in the measured chemistry layer.
Human gene targets engaged by at least one ingredient (measured or predicted).
Biological pathways mapped from those genes.
GTEx tissue compartments used for body-region attribution.
94% of the original 463 species have USDA/FooDB composition; many new ING nodes are nutrition-only or name-only.
New recipe datasets ingested into the v2 store (plus the larger RecipeNLG corpus separately).
97.58% of ingredient mentions in the new recipe corpus resolve to the 695-node universe.
